newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PUMA four tranche bond issue priced.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PUMA four tranche bond issue priced.

text.p: PUMA Management, Macquarie Bank Ltd's securitisaton vehicle, said its A$500 million mortgage backed bond issue has been priced at a weighted average margin over time (WAMOT) of 16.8 basis points over the 90-day bank bill swap rate (BBSW).
This compares with 16.6 basis points for PUMA previous P-6 Series A bonds which were priced in February.

Tranche 1-F from the Masterfund P-6 Series B was priced at 40 basis points over the April 2000 government bond with a coupon of 6.9 percent. The tranche has a face value of A$315 million and is fixed rate until April 15, 2000, and is fungible with trance 1-F of Series A.
Tranche 2, which is floating rate, has a face value of A$135 million and an average expected life of seven years, was priced at 21 basis points over BBSW.
Tranche three, which is floating rate debt, was priced at 22 basis points over BBSW. The issue has an expected average life of 7.3 years and a face value of A$23 million.
Tranche four, which has a face value of A$27 million and an expected average life of 7.3 years, was priced at 34 basis points over.
Tranches one to three are rated AAA/Aaa by Standard & Poor's and Moody's Investors Service, while Tranche 4 is rated AA minus by S&P.
Bonds will be settled on June 13.

"PUMA is the benchmark issuer of mortgage backed securities, evidenced by a maintenance in its funding costs in a market where recent domestic transactions have seen issue nargins increase by between one and two basis points," said Tony Gill, PUMA's managing director

"Pricing achieved for this latest issue reflects strong investor demand for quality PUMA stock. It also reflects the structural enhancements built into our bonds, enhancements which reduce risk for investors," Gill added.
